author: madhva
period: 13th century CE (Madhva's traditional dates are usually given as 1238–1317, though other dates are proposed)
summary: Madhva's concise commentary on the Brahma Sutras, founding the Dvaita school, which holds that God, souls and matter are eternally distinct.
whyRead: Madhva offers the sharpest contrast with Advaita: difference is real and eternal, and God alone is independent. Reading his short commentary alongside Shankara's and Ramanuja's shows the full range of what Vedanta can mean.
questions: Are God and the soul ever identical?

keyTeachings.title: Five differences
keyTeachings.text: Madhva holds that there are real, eternal differences between God and souls, God and matter, soul and soul, soul and matter, and matter and matter (pancha-bheda).

keyTeachings.title: Independent and dependent
keyTeachings.text: Reality divides into the one independent reality, Vishnu, and everything dependent on him.

keyTeachings.title: The world is real
keyTeachings.text: The world is real, not an appearance; knowledge of it is valid.

keyTeachings.title: Grace and devotion
keyTeachings.text: Liberation comes through devotion and God's grace; liberated souls remain distinct from God, enjoying bliss according to their nature.

structure.label: Commentary on all four chapters of the Brahma Sutras
